reason: Glob pattern and cwd come from developer-controlled build configuration in webpack tooling, no untrusted input reaches path resolution.
All text is passed through Convert.string_to_html_entities before being assigned to innerHTML, so embedded HTML is escaped and cannot execute.
The cache file path is built via generateFileLocation($key) inside an internal cache class with no visible untrusted input flowing into the path in the shown code.
Identical cache code: path derived by generateFileLocation from an application-supplied key, no demonstrated attacker-controlled traversal in the snippet.
The snippet is a plain module constructor with no credentials, secrets, or keys anywhere, so hardcoded-credentials claim is inapplicable.
csrf_exempt on REST API endpoints authenticated via API-key header is idiomatic; browser-based CSRF cannot supply the required auth header, so CWE-352 does not apply.
$_REQUEST['almox'] is concatenated directly into the SQL string without any validation, casting, or parameterization, a classic exploitable SQL injection.
ffmpeg commands come from server configuration and the path is substituted as a discrete argv element via exec.Command without a shell, so no code/command injection is possible.
The code performs no outbound HTTP/network requests so SSRF (CWE-918) is inapplicable; its real weaknesses (dynamic local include/dispatch) belong to different CWEs.
Python ElementTree does not resolve external entities by default and the parsed XML is a build-generated distribution file, not attacker-controlled, so XXE does not apply.
